newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc ends lower against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc ends lower against dollar.

text.p: 1500 GMT - The Swiss franc ended lower against the dollar and the mark, with the dollar reviving despite news of a sharp 0.6 percent drop in overall U.S. April producer prices.

One technical analyst said that "fundamentals, for once managed to push the dollar in the direction of what one would interpret" in terms the economy, refering to the dollar's rise on the report. The dollar fell only briefly after the PPI, which quelled participants' expectations for another Federal Reserve interest rate hike. It then gained later in the day.
The dollar was helped as the latest positive inflation news sent U.S. stocks and bonds higher.
Aurel David, technical analyst at Bank Julius Baer, saw the next key level for dollar/Swiss to the upside at 1.4550/4555 Swiss francs.
If that level is taken out, then the next major targets were seen at 1.4685, and 1.4735.

To the downside the major level was 1.4380, with 1.4285 below that. He saw mainly a sideways to upward trend for dollar/Swiss short-term. Overall, he said he was short-term dollar bullish but saw the dollar topping out longer-term.
With respect to dollar/mark, he said "longer-term I don't think we will break 1.7335."
* The dollar ended at 1.4434/4440 Swiss francs on Wednesday, up from 1.4340/4350 francs on Tuesday.
* The mark ended at 84.80/81 Swiss centimes versus 84.40/42 centimes on Tuesday. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
